quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: When loading cargo onto a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Place heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Place lighter items near the front.
Avoid placing items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items in front of the tank bag. Load should go over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can hurt your control of the motorcycle.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may have trouble getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight.
Weave back and forth in your lane.
Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you start riding.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning a curve?

options.text: Only use the front brake.
It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean.
You may have less traction as you lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be careful. When your motorcycle leans into a turn, some tire traction is used for turning. This means less traction is available for stopping.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds above 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.
They happen in the dark.
They involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who have little experience riding their motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Low railroad crossing ahead.
Low clearance ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (in this case, 13 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder.
Ride below the speed limit.
Wear a helmet.
Do not allow a passenger on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single best thing you can do to reduce the risk of head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: How often should you check that your headlight and taillight work?

options.text: Once a month.
Once a week.
Before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always test your lights before you ride. It is important that they work every time you are on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride in a zigzag motion.
Ride on the shoulder instead of on the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is not usually dangerous. If this happens, simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to fight the weaving is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help protect you in a crash?

options.text: A DOT-compliant helmet.
A leather jacket.
A sweatshirt.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sweatshirt.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects against injury. A sweatshirt does not provide the same protection.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Bright colors like red, orange, yellow, and green help other drivers see you. Dark colors like black are harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that traffic will merge from the right side.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in the lane?

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: What does this road sign show?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the recommended safe speed for exiting a highway.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?

options.text: Usually more powerful than a car's headlights.
Usually just as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: What must you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down without coming to a complete stop.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely. Check for pedestrians and traffic crossing the intersection. Wait until it is clear before going.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Maintain your usual space cushion.
Brake later than usual.
Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, making your motorcycle sit lower. Ride slower than usual, especially on curves and bumps. The extra weight means longer braking and acceleration times. Keep a larger space cushion.

questions.question: What is the best way to brake hard in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake, then the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes together for maximum braking power. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks, release the brake pressure right away. Then press the brake again with steady, gentle pressure.

questions.question: What does it feel like if your front tire goes flat?

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
Soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What should you do before every ride?

options.text: Modify the exhaust system.
Clean and adjust your mirrors.
Clean your wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clean and adjust your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, clean your mirrors and adjust them properly. Your mirrors should let you see the road behind you and to the side of you clearly.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep going straight. Brake gently on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
The road that you are on intersects with a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road that you are on intersects with a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or rail.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving your signal on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic light colors from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic light, red is always on top and green is always on bottom. On a horizontal light, red is always on the left and green is always on the right.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride with your headlight on.
Reduce your space cushion.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Leave your headlight on to be more visible at intersections. Ride in a lane position that helps oncoming traffic see you. Keep space around you to avoid danger. Never assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: What should you know about clothing when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not cover your arms or legs completely.
Should not include a jacket if the weather is warm.
Can provide protection in the event of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can provide protection in the event of a crash.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing protects you if you crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothes should fit snugly so they don't flap but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: What colors are signs that show the distance to the next exit on a highway?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Signs that give information about where you are going are green with white letters or pictures.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the portion of the lane that will bring you into other drivers' fields of vision at the earliest possible moment.
Always be in the left lane to be the farthest from oncoming traffic.
Slowly sneak up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight has a better chance of being spotted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the portion of the lane that will bring you into other drivers' fields of vision at the earliest possible moment.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself in the lane so oncoming drivers see you as early as possible. For example, if turning right at a blind corner, stay toward the left side of your lane so a driver can see you sooner.

questions.question: What can help you survive a crash?

options.text: A DOT-compliant helmet.
A baseball cap.
Comfortable shoes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A DOT-compliant helmet.
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT and state standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a proper, secure, quality helmet is the most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: The left
The center
The right
It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This is safest. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may encourage the driver to cut back into your lane too early.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
Your body removes alcohol faster.
The effects of alcohol are less strong.
You are more likely to avoid being pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. It is never safe to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Speed up.
Use only your rear brake.
Avoid sudden moves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden moves on slippery surfaces. Quick changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Move smoothly when speeding up, shifting gears, turning, or braking.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is slippery.
When the sun is shining.
When you expect normal braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs extra time to stop. This applies when the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Do not swerve. Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving may cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: What should a group do if one rider wants to go faster?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a set spot later.
Speed up to keep up with that rider.
Split up and let everyone ride at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a set spot later.
questions.explanation: If one group member wants to ride faster, let them go ahead. Agree to meet at a set location later.

questions.question: What should NOT be part of your pre-ride check?

options.text: A tire check.
A taillight test.
A headlight test.
A paint check.

questions.correctAnswerText: A paint check.
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. Do a full pre-ride inspection before you ride.

questions.question: What kind of boots or shoes should you wear?

options.text: Boots below your ankles.
Boots that cover your ankles.
Soft, flexible footwear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Boots that cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It discourages the driver from cutting in too early.
It encourages the driver to cut in too early.
It encourages the driver to pass quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the driver to cut in too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane when being passed is dangerous. It may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.
